proposals: CPCB should set a published time limit for deciding used-oil EPR registration applications and report monthly how many are granted, under process and incomplete for producers, importers, recyclers and collection agents, so the 94 incomplete and 39 pending producer applications behind only 119 grants become a tracked backlog.

CPCB should publish, for each obligation year, the national EPR target, certificates generated by recyclers, certificates bought by producers and importers, and the shortfall charged Environmental Compensation, so compliance against the 68,946-tonne 2024–25 target can be checked rather than assumed.

CPCB should publish the conversion factors it assigns by recycling technology and the volume-weighted price at which EPR certificates change hands within the 30–100% band, so the market’s actual price signal to re-refiners is visible.

PPAC should split its LOBS/Lube oil import and export line into base oil, finished lubricants and greases, and name the HSN codes it aggregates, so imports of 3,177 thousand tonnes in 2025–26 can be set against what re-refined base oil could actually replace.
